name: Hilium
soft_passes: #3 silhouette: two competing motifs (radial burst + cursor arrow) read as a cluttered asterisk-plus-arrow, nameable but not one clean object
#5 light model: consistent but flat — a diagonal gradient ramp only, no committed top-down lighting
#8 depth: sensible order but near-flat; faint concentric rings are the only spatial cue
failures: #4 16px squint: ~1.5-2.4:1 glyph/field contrast + fine rounded segments smear into a flat cyan tile at Dock/menu-bar size
#7 figure-ground: aqua glyph #00FFFF vs cyan field ~#00ADFF = 1.99:1 (worst 1.46:1 over bright centre, best 2.37:1 over deepest blue), all below 3:1; vanishes in grayscale
#10 variant robustness: not layered for Liquid Glass; separation depends entirely on the cyan field, would collapse under tinted/clear/dark; no dark/mono variant
light_model: Minimal/flat: diagonal gradient ramp (bright cyan upper-left -> blue lower-right), faint top-brighter shading inside strokes; no committed top-down shadow, no baked micro-shadows, no specular
rhymes_hint: generic iOS/utility gradient-squircle + monoline-glyph icons (180px = iOS 60pt@3x, likely reused); connectivity/remote-control utilities with radial signal motifs on cool cyan-blue ramps
notes: 180x180 pre-masked PNG (rounded superellipse already applied, transparent outside) = iOS 60pt@3x size, likely the iOS icon reused for the Mac listing; 1024 full-bleed master and mask-fighting unverifiable, mask discipline judged on render only. Hex values indicative from a small web render, not exact master samples; concentric rings faint enough that some could be compression. Defining flaw is monochrome collapse: glyph and field share one hue, so figure-ground never resolves (1.5-2.4:1 everywhere). Brand mark IS coherent across surfaces (same burst appears white in the cover's bottom-left logo) but the icon's cyan palette does not carry into the cover's austere black/white world (palette-divergent). Not authored as Liquid Glass layers -- a currency gap for macOS 26, not just a contrast one.
